persistence_invariants.brief: A composite unique constraint on (sku, location) so every SKU at every location is uniquely addressable and no two rows share that pair; a collision is rejected at write time (R3).
A CHECK (quantity >= 0) so a stored stock level can never be negative; a pick that would drive it below zero or overcommit is rejected at write time (R2).
sku, location, quantity, and inventory_code are NOT NULL; a stock record cannot be filed missing the identifying or quantity fields (AC1).
Each inventory adjustment row carries a NOT NULL created_at timestamp and actor that are set once and never updated, preserving an unmodifiable audit trail (R1).

Every schema migration is additive and reversible: existing stock records created before a model change survive the migration with no loss, and old reads keep working during rollout (R1, preferences).

nfrs.brief: Existing stock data survives every schema migration with no loss. Each iteration's model change is additive; inventory records created before it are preserved, and every inventory adjustment keeps an unmodifiable created_at timestamp and actor. Defended by PI4/PI5 and a migration-reversibility fitness test that applies migrations to a seeded branch and asserts prior rows remain intact.

Stock levels never go below zero and never overcommit beyond available quantity. Enforced at write time in the service layer (transactional check) and backstopped by the PI2 CHECK constraint; a rejected pick returns a validation error, never a stored negative or a silent double-allocation.

Every SKU at every location is uniquely addressable by (sku, location); no two records share that pair. Resolved at write time via the PI1 composite unique constraint surfaced as a field-named validation error, never two stored duplicates and never an error page.

Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch, never a mock/stub/in-memory substitute. pytest-bdd suites apply Alembic migrations to the branch, exercise the real repository against databricks_postgres, and CI refuses to merge a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch.

The UI is a React + TypeScript single-page application under client/ that loads once and navigates client-side with no full-page reloads; a stock adjustment updates the affected row in place (optimistic, reconciled against the server response). The boundary layer returns JSON only (no server-rendered HTML); the client ships its own component tests while the API is covered by the R4 branch integration tests. Boundary declared renders_via: react.
Validation messages are clear and specific, naming the offending field (not just 'bad request'). Owned at the API boundary as a cross-cutting concern (PO preference).

A stock-level row missing optional detail (par level, batch, serial) still renders cleanly: those default to empty and show an explicit 'not tracked', never a null crash or a blank region (PO preference).

Barcode-scan interactions feel immediate (perceived response under ~200ms from scan event to UI update), achieved via optimistic client-side updates reconciled against the server (PO preference). N/A as a hard server budget; treated as a client-side UX target.
